title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as partnerships form and budgets expand, while launch failures and geopolitical maneuvers add complexity to the landscape. Notably, the recent spaceport finance law could reshape infrastructure investments, and China’s surprise satellite launches signal its growing ambitions.

themes.title: Shifts in Space Infrastructure Finance
themes.body: The new spaceport facility bonds law is poised to fundamentally alter how space infrastructure projects are financed, potentially unlocking new capital flows. This could lead to a more robust and diversified investment landscape in the sector.

themes.title: China's Expanding Satellite Program
themes.body: China's recent surprise launch of the Long March 12B, alongside its test of direct-to-device satellites, highlights its aggressive push in the space race. Such developments may further challenge the U.S. and its allies in terms of technological parity.

themes.title: Challenges in the Launch Market
themes.body: The failure of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket adds to the already constrained launch market, raising concerns about capacity and reliability. As demand for launches grows, these setbacks could have ripple effects on timelines and customer commitments.

themes.title: Defense Budgets and Tech Partnerships
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, underscores the increasing prioritization of space in defense strategy. Meanwhile, partnerships like Anduril and L3Harris on tactical SDA constellation bids signal a trend toward collaborative innovation in defense technology.
